cycle_2_note: Generator (opus) cycle 2: fixed all five Evaluator findings in devcontainer/codex-supervisor.mjs against the AMENDED AC4/AC6/AC7. (1) Terminal state + resume input: adoptState() now carries exitReason through, run() prints 'already complete: <reason>' and returns 0 without spawning, and a resumed run's first input is the literal 'continue' when turns is non-empty (the rewritten prompt only when no turn was ever started). (2) AC7(a) wall deadline while awaiting a turn: new nextNotificationOrDeadline() races the next notification against startedAt+maxWallSeconds — a single unref'd timer on the real clock, a 100 ms poll of the --now-source clock so a virtual advance fires it — then expireDuringTurn() sends turn/interrupt {threadId,turnId}, closes stdin, persists and exits 3. (3) AC7(b) waits capped: recordWait() records the would-be wait in waits[] and throws the ceiling instead of sleeping whenever until > deadline, so both the quota and transient paths are covered. (4) checkGates() gained turnFailures >= maxTurnFailures, and every --max-* below 1 is now a parse-time exit 2. (5) A persisted waits[] entry whose until is still in the future is honoured on resume before anything is sent (sleep, or exit 3 if it ends past the ceiling) — gates run either side of it, all before the server is spawned. Child env, argv, initialize line, REWRITES table and state-file atomicity untouched. The one failure is real, not a test bug: test_codex_supervisor_c2_resume_after_sigterm_sends_continue kills a turn mid-flight (turn/start sent, never completed -> persisted turns: []) and expects the resumed run to send 'continue' per the amended AC4 text ('the literal continue when turns is non-empty... the rewritten prompt only when no turn was ever started'); the actual implementation sent the rewritten prompt ('$vsss go c2') instead, because resumeThread()'s `if (resumed.turns.length) firstText = 'continue'` cannot distinguish 'a turn was attempted and killed before completing' from 'no turn was ever attempted' -- both leave turns: [] on disk with no other persisted marker. python3 code-check.py clean (22 files, shellcheck); python3 smoke-test.py < /dev/null: 4119 checks, 4118 passed, 1 failed, exit 1.
